name: MissingNo.
form: Glitch entity — not a real species

shiny.alt: MissingNo. — no official shiny form exists

dexEntry.text: MissingNo. doesn’t have a real Pokédex entry, because it isn’t a real Pokémon — it’s what happens when Red and Blue are told to display data for a species that was never programmed. Its listed type (Bird, an unused type that behaves identically to Normal), and its height and weight, change depending on exactly how it was encountered, because the game is reading whatever happened to be sitting in memory at the time rather than any fixed stats. Nothing about it was designed on purpose.

funFact.text: Encountering MissingNo. — even without catching it — increases the quantity of whatever item sits in the sixth slot of the player’s Bag by 128, unless it’s already past that number. It’s a side effect of the same memory-overflow bug that lets MissingNo. exist in the first place, not a feature anyone at Game Freak put there on purpose. Nintendo issued a public warning about the glitch in 1999, cautioning that contact with MissingNo. could corrupt save data or Hall of Fame records; strategy guides printed the encounter steps anyway.

firstObtainable.text: Watch the Old Man’s battle tutorial in Viridian City, then Fly directly to Cinnabar Island without triggering another wild encounter first, and Surf along the coastline on the island’s east side. The tutorial temporarily writes the player’s own name into a memory slot normally reserved for wild-Pokémon data, and Cinnabar’s shoreline encounter table reads that leftover data back as a Pokémon — MissingNo.

jackNote: This is the actual reason this whole site is called ItemSixHQ. Not a branding meeting, not a focus group — a Game Boy, the Old Man glitch, and roughly 128 extra Master Balls appearing in slot six like the game owed me money. I have built a hobby, a brand, and apparently a Pokédex entry around a bug. No regrets.

dexEntry.text: The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.

funFact.text: Vileplume's design leans on Rafflesia arnoldii — the real-world record holder for the world's largest flower, also infamous for smelling like rotting meat. Big, toxic and unpleasant to be near: the design brief was clearly followed to the letter.

dexEntry.text: A host-parasite pair in which the parasite mushroom has taken over the host bug. Prefers damp places.

funFact.text: Parasect's design is a real biological horror story in miniature — it's modelled on Cordyceps, real fungi that infect insects, take over their bodies, and eventually kill the host to keep growing. The Pokédex's own "the parasite mushroom has taken over the host bug" line is barely an exaggeration.

dexEntry.text: Its aura becomes stronger when it is frightened or sad, signalling its distress to others.

funFact.text: Riolu’s Diamond & Pearl card (61/130) is a Basic Pokémon with just one attack: Wild Kick. It can deal 30 damage, but a tails flip means it does nothing. A very small lesson in uncertainty.

firstObtainable.text: In Diamond and Pearl, help Riley defeat Team Galactic on Iron Island and he offers you an Egg that hatches into Riolu. This is a gift Egg, not a wild catch.

firstSubstantial.context: A kidnapped Riolu becomes the focus of a rescue story involving Ash and Pokémon Ranger Kellyn; the story continues in Part 2.
